MOLECULAR GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Service

PATIENT INFORMATION
Name: [redacted name]
DOB: [redacted date]
MRN: [redacted ID]
Specimen ID: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Peripheral blood
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

REFERRAL REASON
Testing for genetic susceptibility to breast/ovarian cancer.

METHODOLOGY
Comprehensive BRCA1 and BRCA2 analysis was performed using the following methods:
1. Protein Truncation Test (PTT): Initial screening performed on BRCA1 exon 11 and BRCA2 exons 10 and 11
2. Unidirectional DNA Sequencing: Full coding sequence analysis of BRCA1 (NM_007294.3) and BRCA2 (NM_000059.3) genes including intron/exon boundaries
3. Multiplex Ligation-dependent Probe Amplification (MLPA): Analysis for large deletions and duplications using SALSA MLPA kits P002 (BRCA1) and P045 (BRCA2)

RESULTS

BRCA1 GENE ANALYSIS
Protein Truncation Test: No truncating mutations detected in exon 11
Sequencing: No pathogenic variants identified
MLPA: No deletions or duplications detected
Conclusion: No mutations detected in BRCA1

BRCA2 GENE ANALYSIS
Protein Truncation Test: No truncating mutations detected in exons 10 and 11
Sequencing: HETEROZYGOUS NONSENSE MUTATION IDENTIFIED
  Variant: c.9924C>G
  Protein: p.Tyr3308X
  Location: Exon 27
  Zygosity: Heterozygous
  Classification: Pathogenic
MLPA: No deletions or duplications detected

FINDINGS SUMMARY
A heterozygous nonsense mutation was identified in the BRCA2 gene (c.9924C>G; p.Tyr3308X) in exon 27. This variant introduces a premature stop codon at amino acid position 3308, resulting in a truncated protein lacking 111 amino acids at the C-terminus. This mutation has been previously reported in multiple families with hereditary breast and ovarian cancer and is classified as pathogenic according to ACMG/AMP guidelines.

CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS
The identified BRCA2 nonsense mutation is pathogenic, confirming a diagnosis of inherited breast/ovarian cancer predisposition syndrome. Female carriers of pathogenic BRCA2 mutations have a lifetime risk of breast cancer of 45-85% and ovarian cancer risk of 11-27%. Male carriers have an increased risk of breast cancer (6-8% lifetime risk) and prostate cancer. There may also be increased risks for pancreatic cancer and melanoma.

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Referral to oncology for discussion of risk-reducing strategies and enhanced surveillance protocols
2. Predictive testing is available for family members
3. Genetic counseling is strongly recommended prior to predictive testing of at-risk relatives
4. First-degree relatives have a 50% chance of carrying this mutation
5. Consider referral to high-risk breast clinic for surveillance recommendations

NOMENCLATURE NOTE
Variant nomenclature follows Human Genome Variation Society (HGVS) guidelines. Reference sequences used: BRCA1 (NM_007294.3) and BRCA2 (NM_000059.3).

DATA VERIFICATION
All positive findings have been confirmed by repeat analysis. This test was developed and validated by the [redacted location] Molecular Genetics Laboratory.

Authorized by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director
